#schema: # Split rule: references/tool-declaration-policy.md
# koto drives the plan-level loop: init lifts the execute template, next
# submits the tasks array and the finalization evidence. `next` also carries
# --no-cleanup on every tick, so the tick that reaches paused_for_review or
# another success terminal keeps the session's context instead of deleting it
# (references/koto-session-retention.md). context add/get carry the settled
# branch and the per-child batch view, and status reports progress. `context
# add` pipes on stdin for the settled-branch write and the drift-facts writes
# of plan_intent.md and drift_facts.json; the lead shape's `step_refine/<step>.md`
# record, written by the owning session between steps in both templates, is
# `context add --from-file`.
# `koto workflows --children` is the owning session's in the lead shape: it
# names each step's child from the list in spawn_and_await, and after a lost
# context it names the children whose `koto status` it reads (SKILL.md, and
# the coordinated template's step-agent handoff). A later /work-on child runs
# the same call in its analysis to find its predecessors' summaries.
# The completion cascade's script owns the shirabe side. It lives under /work-on
# (skills/work-on/scripts/run-cascade.sh), which runs it for a standalone issue,
# and plan_completion reaches it over a cross-skill path; these records stay
# because /execute still runs it and its preflight must find the tools. It
# probes and re-verifies the
# chain with `validate --lifecycle-chain --format json --mode=ready`, adding
# `--allow-untracked-acs` when WORK_ON_ALLOW_UNTRACKED_ACS=1 suppresses L06;
# it then runs `finalize-chain` over the PLAN's upstream and falls back to
# `transition <plan> Done`. SKILL.md's visibility boundary routes the
# governance-aware checks with `--visibility`.
# pr_finalization's owned_pr_body_conformant gate runs /work-on's
# check-pr-output.sh on every plan, which calls `validate --pr-body
# --pr-title --format --writing-style`, so those flags are always records too.
# Its deferral_recorded gate runs shared-deferral-record.sh on every plan:
# `koto workflows --children` lists the run's children, and
# `koto context exists`/`get` read each one's verification_deferral. When the
# run or a child deferred verification, it runs check-pr-output.sh
# --deferral-record --owned, which reads the owned PR's body with `gh pr view`
# and jq. Each falls under the koto, gh and jq records below. execute-open.sh
# sources scripts/lib/verification-deferral.sh, whose reason checks use jq.
# On a coordinated plan node-push.sh runs the same script over a node's named
# children (`--child`, read in the node worktree with `--child-dir`), with the
# same koto, gh and jq calls and no `koto workflows`, and records their
# reasons in run/node. The loop (coord-common.sh) runs it with those reasons
# (`--recorded`), making no koto call. A node record written before the
# reasons were recorded has its children read where they are bound: `koto
# session list` gives each one's execution directory, and the script reads it
# there with `--child-dir`; the same listing finds the children when the PLAN
# is gone. child-read.sh runs the
# owning session's `koto status` and `koto context get` of a work item in the
# node worktree.
# The coordinated path adds the two coordination modes of the same subcommand:
# `--coordination-body` for offline authoring feedback on the PR body, and
# `--merge-gate` for the live merge-last gate. Neither runs on a single-pr
# plan, which is why they are a mode record rather than part of the always one.
# That record is not checked at load. SKILL.md's Input Modes section verifies
# it with `skill-preflight.sh execute --mode coordinated`, right after the
# execution_mode enum re-validates and before the loop dispatches a child.
# gh drives the home PR throughout (pr list, pr create, pr edit, pr ready, pr
# checks, pr view, issue view) and the opt-in merge: merge-verdict.sh reads
# the PR, its checks, and the base's rules through `pr view`, `pr checks`, and
# `api`, and merge-exec.sh makes the repository's one `pr merge` call. git
# creates and pushes the shared branch and stages the cascade's transitions,
# and fetches, diffs, and merges origin/main in for the drift check; jq builds the cascade
# report and the drift facts; python3 is
# the portable realpath in run-cascade.sh.
# (`--pr-body` in the template only names what CI enforces, but node-push.sh
# runs it, so the mode record below declares it and no exemption is needed.)
# The koto floor. /execute enters its orchestrator session through
# skills/execute/scripts/execute-open.sh and the shared scripts/koto-open.sh,
# which is the call site for `koto init --vars-file`, `--attach-live`,
# `--replace-terminal`, and `--koto-leg`. Those flags exist only in koto
# 0.13.0 and later, and so do the template's result maps, transition
# context_assignments, constrained and rebindable variables, and
# `overridable: false` gates, so the `koto init` record below is /execute's
# declared koto floor: the tool-declaration policy allows no version number
# here, and preflight on an older koto names these missing flags and the install
# route instead. As with run-cascade.sh's records, the call site lives in a
# shared script, which the one-directional requires check does not treat as a
# finding.
# The records catch a koto older than 0.13.0 only. shirabe's koto minimum is
# 0.22.0 (scripts/assert-koto-floor.sh). What 0.14.0 added (a failure terminal
# keeps its session, and a child's result is delivered under --no-cleanup) is
# behaviour with no flag to declare, so no record here carries it. The preflight
# compares koto's version with that minimum at load instead
# (scripts/lib/preflight-minimum.sh), and CI tests it.
# The merge step adds calls without new flags. record-merge-verdict.sh clears
# its keys with `koto context remove` and reads `expected_head` with
# `koto context get`; push-and-record.sh and `run-cascade.sh --push --session`
# write `expected_head` with `koto context add`; record-write-set.sh and
# adopt-or-create-pr.sh write `repos`, `home_pr`, and `waiting` the same way;
# print-exit.sh renders the result `koto status` reports. On the gh side,
# owned-pr.sh reads `gh api user`, `gh api repos/<repo>`, and `gh pr list`,
# and makes one `gh pr edit --body-file` on a --take-over;
# run-id.sh reads the run identity (and, from the session-opening scripts,
# mints it) with `koto context exists`,
# `koto context get`, and `koto context add`, and od reads /dev/urandom;
# record-write-set.sh falls back to `gh repo view`; adopt-or-create-pr.sh makes
# the one `gh pr create --draft`; merge-exec.sh the one `gh pr merge`.
# owned_ci_passing's fallback, /work-on's ci-cancel-after-merge.sh --owned,
# reads `gh pr view`, `gh pr checks`, and `gh api repos/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>`,
# and writes ci_cancelled_after_merge.txt with `koto context add`. Its last
# fallback, /work-on's ci-none-declared.sh --owned, reads
# `gh api repos/<repo>/contents/<path>`, `gh pr checks`, and `gh pr view`, and
# writes ci_none_declared.txt with `koto context add`. git adds
# `ls-remote --symref` and the explicit-refspec push in push-and-record.sh. All
# of those fall under the gh, git, and jq records.
# The coordinated envelope (execute-coordinated.md) adds one koto verb: the run
# record's reader (run-record-lib.sh, sourced by coord-common.sh,
# run-record.sh, and execute-open.sh) lists a session's `run/` keys with
# `koto context list --prefix run/`, a coordinated-mode record below.
# record-coord-setup.sh, record-coordination-verdict.sh, coord-merge.sh, and
# run-record.sh otherwise read and write context with
# `koto context get/add/remove/exists`. Its scripts add gh
# and git calls under the same records: node-push.sh's node-PR
# `gh pr create --draft`, coord-render.sh's `gh pr edit --body-file` of the
# coordination body, record-coord-setup.sh's `gh pr edit --body-file` of the
# node PRs it stamps on a recovery given --adopt-run, and `gh pr ready`;
# execute-open.sh's read-only `git log` and `git show` of a deleted PLAN's
# last version; node-cut.sh's `git worktree add` and

# they run: coord-render.sh validates each rendered coordination body with

# `--pr-body` and `--pr-title`, and coord-merge.sh and the loop's
# evaluate-coordination step run `--merge-gate --mode=ready` with one `--pr`
# per indexed ref.
